questions.question: The winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature for 2025, author László Krasznahorkai, belongs to which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hungary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **László Krasznahorkai** is a renowned novelist and screenwriter who was awarded the **2025 Nobel Prize in Literature**.
 
• He was born on **January 5, 1954**, in the town of **Gyula**, located in southeastern **Hungary**.
 
• The **Swedish Academy** cited his "compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art" as the primary motivation for the prestigious award.
 
• With this achievement, **Krasznahorkai** became the second **Hungarian** author to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, following **Imre Kertész**, who was honored in **2002**.
 
• His writing is globally recognized for its **postmodern** depth, often utilizing extremely long sentences and exploring **dystopian** and **melancholic** themes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Major Literary Contributions and Style:
 
 
• His debut novel, **Sátántangó** (1985), is a landmark of **Hungarian** literature and was later adapted into a legendary seven-hour film by the director **Béla Tarr**.
 
• Other notable works include **The Melancholy of Resistance** (1989), **War & War** (1999), and **Baron Wenckheim's Homecoming** (2016), the latter of which won the **National Book Award for Translated Literature** in **2019**.
 
• The author's unique prose style, described as 'reality examined to the point of madness', features flowing language that often spans several pages without a single full stop.
 
• In **2015**, he was awarded the **Man Booker International Prize**, solidifying his status as one of the most important living writers in the world.
 
 
 
• Context of the **Nobel Prize**:
 
 
• The **Nobel Prize in Literature** has been awarded since **1901** to individuals who have produced the most outstanding work in an ideal direction.
 
• The prize includes a gold medal, a diploma, and a monetary award, which in **2025** was valued at approximately **11 million Swedish kronor**.

questions.question: What is the function of the keyboard shortcut Alt + F10?

options.text: Selects the active tab on the Ribbon and shows access keys

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Selects the active tab on the Ribbon and shows access keys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Microsoft Office** applications, specifically within **Word for the Web** and certain web-based productivity suites, the **Alt + F10** keyboard shortcut is used to move the keyboard focus to the **Ribbon**.
 
• Once this shortcut is triggered, the interface displays **Access Keys** (also known as **Key Tips**), which are alphanumeric overlays that allow users to navigate through tabs and commands using only the keyboard.
 
• This function is vital for **accessibility**, adhering to **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)**, as it provides a reliable method for users with motor impairments to access complex menu structures without a mouse.
 
• While the standalone **F10** or **Alt** keys perform a similar function in desktop versions, **Alt + F10** is the designated combination in web environments to prevent conflicts with native **browser-level shortcuts**.
 
• In modern **collaborative platforms**, this shortcut ensures that the focus is placed directly on the primary navigation element, enabling rapid execution of formatting and editing tools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maximizes the current window**:

 
 
• In legacy **Windows** applications and older **Microsoft Word** versions, **Alt + F10** was the standard shortcut to toggle the **maximize** state of the program window.
 
• In contemporary **Excel** and **PowerPoint** desktop apps, this combination is also used to toggle the **Selection Pane**, which manages the visibility and layering of **graphic objects**.
 
 
 
• **Opens the Help menu**:
 
 
• The universal function key for accessing **Help** documentation, support search, or **Office Assistant** features is **F1**.
 
 
 
• **Closes the document**:
 
 
• Common shortcuts for closing the active document or file without exiting the application include **Ctrl + W** or **Ctrl + F4**.
 
• In contrast, **Alt + F4** is used to terminate and close the entire **application window**.

questions.question: Which memory is fastest and located very close to the CPU?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cache Memory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cache memory** is an extremely high-speed, volatile computer memory that provides high-speed data access to the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**.
 
• It is physically located directly on the **CPU chip** or connected via a dedicated high-speed bus, making it the fastest memory in the hierarchy after **CPU registers**.
 
• The primary function of **Cache** is to store frequently used program instructions and data that the **CPU** is likely to need next, acting as a buffer between the **CPU** and the slower **Main Memory (RAM)**.
 
• It operates on **SRAM (Static Random Access Memory)** technology, which is faster and more expensive than the **DRAM (Dynamic RAM)** used for standard system memory.
 
• Modern processors typically feature multiple levels of cache, known as **L1, L2, and L3 Cache**, where **L1** is the smallest and fastest, located closest to the processor cores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hard Disk**:

 
 
• It is a **Secondary Storage** device that uses **magnetic storage** to store and retrieve digital information.
 
• While it offers large storage capacities, it is significantly slower than **Cache** due to its mechanical nature involving spinning platters and moving heads.
 
 
 
• **Pen Drive**:
 
 
• A portable **Solid-State** storage device that uses **Flash memory** and interfaces with the computer through a **USB port**.
 
• It is **Non-volatile** and much slower than internal system memory components like **Cache** or **RAM**.
 
 
 
• **CD-ROM**:
 
 
• Stands for **Compact Disc Read-Only Memory**, which is a type of **Optical Storage** medium.
 
• Data is recorded and read using **laser beams**, and it has the slowest data transfer rate among the given options.

questions.question: As per RTI Rules 2012, a person below poverty line is liable to pay what amount as application fee to file an RTI?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Right to Information (RTI) Rules, 2012**, notified by the **Central Government**, govern the fees and procedures for filing applications under the **RTI Act, 2005**.
 
• According to **Rule 5** of the **RTI Rules 2012**, no fee under **Rule 3** (application fee) and **Rule 4** (fees for providing information) shall be charged from any person who is **Below Poverty Line (BPL)**.
 
• The **proviso to Section 7(5)** of the **Right to Information Act, 2005** also explicitly mandates that persons belonging to the **BPL category**, as determined by the appropriate government, are exempted from paying any fees.
 
• To claim this exemption, the applicant must provide a copy of their **BPL certificate** or a valid proof of identity issued by a competent authority along with the **RTI application**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fee Structure for General Applicants**:

 
 
• **Application Fee**: For individuals not in the BPL category, the standard application fee is **₹10**.
 
• **Cost of Information**: Fees include **₹2** for each page (A-4 or A-3 size) and actual cost/price for samples or models.
 
• **Electronic Media**: Information provided in **diskettes or floppies** costs **₹50** per unit.
 
 
 
• **Operational Framework**:
 
 
• **Payment Modes**: Fees can be paid via **Cash**, **Demand Draft**, **Bankers Cheque**, or **Indian Postal Order (IPO)**.
 
• **Response Timeline**: The **Public Information Officer (PIO)** must provide the information within **30 days**, or **48 hours** if it concerns the **life or liberty** of a person.
 
• **Appellate Authority**: If the information is denied or delayed, the applicant can file a **First Appeal** within **30 days**.

questions.question: During which of the following revolutions in India did planned investment in horticulture become highly productive, leading to the emergence of the sector as a sustainable livelihood option?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Golden Revolution** in India took place between **1991 and 2003**, a period marked by a massive surge in the production of **horticulture**, **honey**, and **fruits**.
 
• During this phase, planned investments in the **horticultural sector** were prioritized to enhance productivity, helping India emerge as a global leader in the production of **bananas**, **mangoes**, and various **spices**.
 
• The revolution played a crucial role in diversifying Indian agriculture, shifting the focus from traditional food grains to high-value crops, thereby making horticulture a **sustainable livelihood option** for many farmers by increasing rural income and export potential.
 
• **Nirpakh Tutej** is considered the **Father of the Golden Revolution** in India due to his significant contributions to the growth of this sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blue Revolution**

 
 
• This revolution focused on the exponential growth of the **fisheries** and **aquaculture** sector.
 
• It was launched during the **Seventh Five-Year Plan** (1985−1990) to improve the economic condition of fish farmers through the **Fish Farmers Development Agency (FFDA)**.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**
 
 
• Initiated in the **mid-1960s**, it aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in **food grains**, specifically **wheat** and **rice**.
 
• It involved the use of **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds**, chemical fertilizers, and modern irrigation techniques, led by **M.S. Swaminathan** in India.
 
 
 
• **White Revolution**
 
 
• Also known as **Operation Flood**, it was launched in **1970** to transform India from a milk-deficient nation to the world's largest milk producer.
 
• **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, the founder of **Amul**, is known as the **Father of the White Revolution**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a prominent language of the Indo-Aryan family?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kurukh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indo-Aryan** language family is a major sub-branch of the **Indo-European** family, spoken by approximately **78 percent** of the Indian population. It includes prominent languages like **Hindi**, **Bengali**, **Urdu**, **Punjabi**, **Marathi**, and **Gujarati**.
 
• **Hindi** is a premier **Indo-Aryan** language written in the **Devanagari** script. It serves as one of the official languages of the **Union of India** and is primarily spoken in the **Hindi Belt** of Northern and Central India.
 
• **Bengali** is the second most spoken language in India, belonging to the **Eastern Indo-Aryan** group. It evolved from **Magadhi Prakrit** and is the official language of **West Bengal** and **Tripura**.
 
• **Urdu** is an **Indo-Aryan** language that developed in **North India**. While it shares a nearly identical grammar and base vocabulary with Hindi (forming **Hindustani**), it is distinguished by its **Perso-Arabic** script and heavy lexical influence from **Persian** and **Arabic**.
 
• **Kurukh** (also known as **Oraon**) is NOT an Indo-Aryan language. It belongs to the **Dravidian** language family, specifically the **North Dravidian** subgroup. It is spoken by the **Oraon** and **Kisan** tribes in **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Odisha**, and **West Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kurukh Language:**

 
 
• **Subgroup:** It is closely related to the **Malto** language of the **Rajmahal Hills** and **Brahui** spoken in **Pakistan**, forming the northernmost branch of the **Dravidian** family.
 
• **Official Status:** In **2017**, the state of **West Bengal** granted **Kurukh** the status of an official language.
 
• **Script:** It is traditionally written in the **Devanagari** script, but an indigenous script called **Tolong Siki** was developed by **Dr. Narayan Oraon** in **1999** for the language.
 
• **UNESCO Status:** The language is listed in **UNESCO’s Atlas of the World’s Languages in Danger** as a **vulnerable** language.
 
 
 
• **Language Families in India:**
 
 
• **Dravidian:** Primarily concentrated in the South, including **Tamil**, **Telugu**, **Kannada**, and **Malayalam**, as well as tribal pockets like **Gondi** and **Kurukh**.
 
• **Austroasiatic:** Includes tribal languages such as **Santhali**, **Munda**, and **Khasi**.
 
• **Sino-Tibetan:** Includes languages of the **Himalayan** region and **North-East India** like **Manipuri** and **Bodo**.

questions.question: Which category of beneficiaries is eligible for ₹1 lakh under Telangana’s Revanth Anna ka Sahara-Miskeen la Kosam scheme launched in September 2025?

• The **Revanth Anna ka Sahara-Miskeen la Kosam** scheme is a flagship social welfare initiative launched by the **Government of Telangana** in **September 2025** under the leadership of Chief Minister **Anumula Revanth Reddy**.
 
• The term **Miskeen** is derived from Arabic and Urdu, signifying the **destitute** or the **needy**, while **la Kosam** is a Telugu phrase meaning **for the sake of**, highlighting the inclusive nature of the state's administration.
 
• The scheme provides a one-time financial assistance of **₹1,00,000 (1 Lakh)** to **economically weak Muslim families** to help them overcome financial distress and improve their standard of living.
 
• It specifically targets individuals and households listed under the **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** category within the minority community, ensuring that the benefits reach the most marginalized sections of society.
 
• The **Minority Welfare Department** of Telangana serves as the nodal agency for the implementation, verification, and disbursement of funds through **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT recommended by the 73rd Indian Constitutional Amendment Act?

options.text: Establishment of Zila panchayat at district level
Establishment of Finance Commission of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Establishment of Finance Commission of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which came into effect on **April 24, 1993**, inserted **Part IX** (The Panchayats) and the **Eleventh Schedule** into the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The Act mandated the **establishment of a three-tier structure** of **Panchayati Raj** in every state with a population over 20 lakhs, comprising the **Gram Panchayat** (village level), **Panchayat Samiti** (intermediate level), and **Zila Panchayat** (district level).
 
• Under **Article 243-I**, the Act recommended the **Establishment of State Finance Commissions** by the Governor of every state to review the financial position of local bodies and recommend the distribution of tax revenues.
 
• The **Establishment of Zila Panchayat at the district level** was a core recommendation to ensure decentralized governance and local self-government at the highest administrative level of a district.
 
• The **Finance Commission of India** was established under **Article 280** of the Constitution in **1951**; its origin is independent of and predates the **73rd Amendment Act**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 280 (Finance Commission of India)**:

 
 
• It is a **quasi-judicial body** constituted by the **President of India** every five years.
 
• Its primary role is to define the financial relations between the **Union Government** and the **State Governments**.
 
• The **73rd Amendment** only added a clause to **Article 280** requiring the central commission to recommend measures to augment the **Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement the resources of **Panchayats**.
 
 
 
• **Mandatory Provisions of the 73rd Amendment**:
 
 
• Organization of **Gram Sabha** in a village or group of villages.
 
• Direct elections to all seats in **Panchayats** at all levels.
 
• Reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in proportion to their population.
 
• Mandatory **one-third reservation for women** in seats and chairperson posts.
 
• Fixing a uniform **five-year term** for all levels of **Panchayati Raj Institutions**.

questions.question: A doctor prescribes a lens with a power of P=−2.5 D to a patient. This lens is _____.

options.text: A convex lens, used to correct Myopia.
A concave lens, used to correct Hypermetropia.
A concave lens, used to correct Myopia.
A convex lens, used to correct Hypermetropia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A concave lens, used to correct Myopia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power of a lens is mathematically defined as the reciprocal of its **focal length** (f) expressed in meters (P = 1/f). The standard **S.I. unit** for lens power is the **Dioptre (D)**.
 
• According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, a lens with **negative power** (such as **-2.5 D**) possess a **negative focal length**, which specifically identifies it as a **concave lens** or **diverging lens**.
 
• **Myopia**, commonly referred to as **nearsightedness**, is a refractive error where parallel light rays from a distant object converge at a point in front of the **retina** rather than directly upon it.
 
• A **concave lens** is utilized to correct **Myopia** because it diverges the incoming light rays before they reach the eye lens, effectively shifting the focal point further back so that the image is perfectly formed on the **retina**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypermetropia** (Farsightedness):

 
 
• This vision defect occurs when a person can see distant objects clearly, but nearby objects appear blurred because the image is formed **behind the retina**.
 
• It is corrected using a **convex lens**, also known as a **converging lens**, which has a **positive power** and **positive focal length**.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens**:
 
 
• Characterized by being thicker in the middle than at the edges.
 
• It converges light rays and is used in applications like **magnifying glasses**, **microscopes**, and to correct **presbyopia**.
 
 
 
• **Calculation**:
 
 
• For the given power **P = -2.5 D**, the focal length is f = 1/P = 1/(-2.5) = **-0.4 meters** or **-40 cm**.

questions.question: What was the impact of the 1990s' reforms on India's economic growth?

options.text: They led to more sustainable growth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They led to more sustainable growth.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The economic reforms initiated in **1991**, often referred to as the **LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** model, were triggered by a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis**.
 
• Prior to these reforms, the Indian economy was characterized by the **Licence Raj** and a slow growth rate often termed the **Hindu Rate of Growth**, which averaged around 3.5% annually between the 1950s and 1980s.
 
• Post-1991, India witnessed a significant transition toward a **market-oriented economy**, which led to an increase in **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** growth rates, often exceeding 6–7% in the subsequent decades.
 
• The reforms promoted **sustainable growth** by diversifying the economic base, increasing the role of the **services sector**, and enhancing the **Foreign Exchange Reserves** from a mere 1.2 billion USD in 1991 to robust levels that protected the economy from external shocks.
 
• The structural adjustments reduced government intervention and encouraged **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, making the growth trajectory more resilient and less dependent on debt-led financing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 1991 reforms were spearheaded by Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and then-Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.

 
 
• **Liberalization:** Involved the abolition of industrial licensing for most sectors and the **deregulation** of the private sector.
 
• **Privatization:** Focused on **disinvestment** in public sector undertakings (PSUs) to improve efficiency and reduce the fiscal burden on the state.
 
• **Globalization:** Aimed at integrating the Indian economy with the world through the reduction of **import tariffs** and the removal of quantitative restrictions on trade.
 
• **Financial Sector Reforms:** Included the establishment of **SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)** as a statutory body in **1992** to regulate the capital markets.
 
• **Fiscal Policy:** Efforts were made to curb the **fiscal deficit** and reform the tax structure to widen the tax base.

questions.question: The Goa Carnival is primarily associated with which of the following cultural or religious traditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christian tradition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Goa Carnival** is a world-renowned festival that was introduced to the Indian subcontinent by the **Portuguese** during their colonial rule in the **18th century**.
 
• The festival is intrinsically linked to the **Catholic Christian** liturgical calendar, serving as a **pre-Lenten** celebration held for four days prior to **Ash Wednesday**.
 
• The term **Carnival** is derived from the **Latin** words **Carne Vale**, which translates to 'farewell to meat', marking the final period of indulgence before the **40-day** period of fasting and penance known as **Lent**.
 
• The celebration is traditionally presided over by **King Momo**, a character based on the **Greek** god of mockery, who decrees that his subjects should eat, drink, and be merry (**Kha, Piye ani Majja Kar**).

questions.question: Which of the following is the most widely used irrigation method in India?

The correct answer is __**Surface irrigation**__.

__
 
• **Surface irrigation** is the most common and traditional method used in **India**, where water is distributed over the soil surface by **gravity**.
 
• It accounts for more than **90%** of the total irrigated area in the country due to its low initial cost and simplicity of operation.
 
• The primary techniques under this category include **Flood irrigation**, **Basin irrigation**, **Furrow irrigation**, and **Border irrigation**.
 
• This method is widely practiced in the **Indo-Gangetic Plains**, particularly for water-intensive crops like **Rice**, **Wheat**, and **Sugarcane**.
 
• The water for surface irrigation is primarily sourced from extensive **Canal networks**, **Tanks**, and **Tube wells**.

• **Sprinkler irrigation**:
 
 
• Water is sprayed into the air through nozzles, mimicking **Natural rainfall**.
 
• It is highly effective for **Sandy soils** and uneven terrains where surface leveling is difficult.
 
 
 
• **Subsurface irrigation**:
 
 
• Water is applied below the soil surface through a network of **Perforated pipes** or buried drip lines.
 
• This method minimizes **Surface evaporation** and is often used for high-value commercial crops.

questions.question: Which community lost its constitutional provision of nominated representation in legislatures through the 104th Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anglo-Indians**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019** was enacted to amend **Article 334** of the **Constitution of India**, which regulates the period of reservation for certain communities in the legislatures.
 
• The amendment extended the reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies** for another **10 years**, until **January 25, 2030**.
 
• Significantly, the Act did not extend the provision for the nomination of members from the **Anglo-Indian community** to the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• Under **Article 331**, the **President** of India previously had the power to nominate **two members** of the **Anglo-Indian** community to the **Lok Sabha** if they were not adequately represented.
 
• Similarly, under **Article 333**, the **Governor** of a State could nominate **one member** of the **Anglo-Indian** community to the **State Legislative Assembly**.
 
• As this provision was not renewed by the **104th Amendment**, the special representation for **Anglo-Indians** effectively ceased on **January 25, 2020**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anglo-Indian Definition**:

 
 
• According to **Article 366(2)**, an **Anglo-Indian** is a person whose father or any of whose other male progenitors in the male line is or was of **European descent** but who is domiciled within the territory of India.
 
• The **Union Government** justified the removal of their nomination by stating that the community has integrated well and their population does not necessitate reserved seats.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Context**:
 
 
• The amendment was introduced as the **126th Constitutional Amendment Bill** in **December 2019** and received the **President's assent** in **January 2020**.
 
• The **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** continue to enjoy seat reservations based on their population proportion to ensure political inclusivity in the **world's largest democracy**.

questions.question: Which of the following types of weathering is common in areas with large temperature differences between day and night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exfoliation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exfoliation** is a form of **mechanical weathering** that is particularly dominant in **arid** and **semi-arid regions** where the **diurnal range of temperature** (the difference between maximum day and minimum night temperatures) is extremely high.
 
• During the day, intense solar radiation causes the **outer layers** of the rock to heat up and **expand**. Because rocks are **poor conductors of heat**, this thermal expansion does not penetrate deep into the interior, creating internal **differential stress**.
 
• At night, as temperatures plummet, these surface layers **contract** rapidly. The repeated cycle of **thermal expansion and contraction** over thousands of years weakens the structural integrity of the rock's surface.
 
• Eventually, the outer shells or 'skins' of the rock break away in thin, concentric sheets. This process is frequently referred to as **onion-skin weathering** due to the way the rock peels in layers.
 
• This phenomenon is common in **granitic rocks** and often results in the formation of large, rounded landforms known as **exfoliation domes**, such as those found in the **Sierra Nevada** mountains or the **Enchanted Rock** in Texas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbonation**

 
 
• It is a **chemical weathering** process where **carbon dioxide** from the atmosphere reacts with rainwater to form **carbonic acid** (H₂CO₃).
 
• This weak acid reacts with **calcium carbonate** in rocks like **limestone** and **marble**, converting them into soluble **calcium bicarbonate**, which is then washed away.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation**
 
 
• This occurs when **oxygen** in the atmosphere or water reacts with certain minerals, particularly those containing **iron**.
 
• The process transforms **ferrous iron** into **ferric iron** (rusting), which weakens the rock structure and gives it a characteristic **reddish-brown** or yellowish hue.
 
 
 
• **Solution**
 
 
• This is the simplest form of **chemical weathering** where certain minerals are directly **dissolved** in water.
 
• It is highly effective on **rock salt** (halite) and **gypsum**, where the mineral ions are separated and carried away in a liquid state, leaving voids in the rock.

While the Guptas ruled from **Pataliputra**, the **Maukharis** established their political base at **Kannauj** (ancient Kanyakubja), marking a significant shift in the geopolitical center of North India.

questions.question: Which of the following economic models formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan?

• The **Second Five-Year Plan**, which spanned from **1956 to 1961**, was based on the economic framework developed by the renowned Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
• The **Mahalanobis model** shifted the focus of Indian planning from agriculture to **rapid industrialization**, specifically prioritizing the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
• The core philosophy of this model was that investment in **capital goods** (such as steel, chemicals, and machine-building) would provide the necessary infrastructure for long-term economic growth and **self-reliance**.
 
• Under this plan, the **Public Sector** was assigned a leading role in the economy to drive industrial expansion and achieve a **Socialistic Pattern of Society**, as envisioned during the **Avadi Session** of the Indian National Congress in **1955**.
 
• Five major **Steel Plants** were established during this period with foreign assistance, including those at **Bhilai**, **Durgapur**, and **Rourkela**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**:

 
 
• This model served as the foundation for the **First Five-Year Plan (1951−1956)**.
 
• It emphasized increasing the **rate of savings** and focused primarily on the **agricultural sector** and **irrigation** projects to address food shortages.
 
 
 
• **Neo-classical minimal-state model**:
 
 
• This economic perspective advocates for **free markets** and limited government intervention, which was contrary to the **state-led industrialization** strategy of the Second Plan.
 
 
 
• **Economic Targets**:
 
 
• The **Second Plan** aimed for a **25 percent** increase in the national income to raise the standard of living.
 
• It also saw the establishment of the **Atomic Energy Commission** in **1958**, led by **Homi J. Bhabha**.

questions.question: The fibrous root system, in which the primary root is short-lived and replaced by numerous adventitious roots, is a characteristic feature of which group of plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monocotyledonous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Monocotyledonous** plants, the **primary root** is **short-lived** and is soon replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the **base of the stem**.
 
• These roots constitute the **fibrous root system**, which forms a dense network of thin, moderately branching roots that spread out near the soil surface.
 
• This system is essential for providing firm **anchorage** to the plant and ensuring efficient **absorption** of water and minerals from the upper layers of the soil.
 
• Common examples of plants exhibiting this characteristic include **Wheat**, **Maize**, **Rice**, **Barley**, and various types of **Grasses**.
 
• Unlike the taproot system, the fibrous system does not have a single dominant central axis; instead, all roots are approximately equal in thickness and length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dicotyledonous**

 
 
• These plants typically possess a **taproot system**.
 
• The **primary root** is a direct elongation of the **radicle** and persists throughout the plant life, giving rise to lateral roots like **secondary** and **tertiary roots**.
 
• Examples include **Mustard**, **Gram**, and **Pea** plants.
 
 
 
• **Gymnosperms**
 
 
• Most **Gymnosperms** generally have a **taproot system**.
 
• In some genera, roots have symbiotic associations, such as **Mycorrhiza** in **Pinus** or **coralloid roots** in **Cycas** associated with **nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria**.
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes**
 
 
• In **Pteridophytes**, the primary root is **ephemeral** (short-lived).
 
• It is replaced by **adventitious roots** that arise from the **rhizome** or stem, providing necessary nutrients to the sporophyte.

questions.question: 'Effect of Proclamation of Emergency' is explicitly provided in which of the following provisions of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 353**__.

__
 
• **Article 353** of the **Constitution of India** explicitly outlines the **Effect of Proclamation of Emergency**. It details how the administrative and legislative machinery of the country shifts from a federal to a more unitary structure during a **National Emergency**.
 
• Under **Article 353(a)**, the executive power of the **Union** extends to giving directions to any **State** regarding the manner in which the State's executive power is to be exercised. This essentially brings the State administration under the total control of the **Central Government**.
 
• Under **Article 353(b)**, the legislative power of **Parliament** is expanded. It gains the authority to make laws on subjects mentioned in the **State List** (List II), which are normally under the exclusive jurisdiction of the States.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** further expanded the scope of **Article 353**, allowing the executive directions and legislative power of the Union to extend to States other than the one where the **Emergency** is specifically in operation, provided the security of India is threatened.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Pertains to the **Language** to be used in representations for redress of grievances.
 
• It ensures every person has the right to submit a representation in any language used in the **Union** or the **State**.

• **Article 252**:
 
 
• Describes the power of **Parliament** to legislate for two or more States by **consent**.
 
• If the legislatures of two or more States pass resolutions requesting Parliament to regulate a matter in the **State List**, Parliament can enact such a law for those specific States.

questions.question: In the process of ecological succession, the entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area are called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Sere** refers to the entire sequence of biotic communities that replace one another in a given area over a period of time during the process of **ecological succession**.
 
• **Ecological succession** is defined as the orderly and predictable change in the species composition of a given area, eventually leading to a stable community.
 
• The individual transitional communities within a **sere** are referred to as **seral stages** or **seral communities**.
 
• In successive **seral stages**, there is typically an increase in the number of species, a change in the **diversity** of organisms, and an overall increase in the total **biomass** of the ecosystem.
 
• A **Sere** represents the complete chronological progression of life, starting from the first organisms to inhabit a bare area (the **pioneer community**) to the final, stable state (the **climax community**).
 
• These changes are driven by both **biological factors** (interaction between species) and **physical factors** (alterations in soil, light, and moisture conditions caused by the organisms themselves).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climax Community**:

 
 
• This is the final, relatively stable stage of **ecological succession** that is in near equilibrium with the **regional climate**.
 
• Unlike **seral stages**, the **climax community** remains essentially unchanged as long as environmental conditions are constant.
 
 
 
• **Ecesis**:
 
 
• This is a vital stage in the process of **succession** that involves the successful establishment of a species in a new area.
 
• It includes the **germination**, growth, and **reproduction** of the migrating species after they reach a new territory.
 
 
 
• **Invasion**:
 
 
• This represents the entire process of a species entering and establishing itself in a **bare area** (Nudation).
 
• It is comprised of three distinct steps: **Migration** (dispersal of seeds or spores), **Ecesis** (establishment), and **Aggregation** (increase in population density).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes eutrophication?

options.text: Mixing of cold and warm water currents in oceans
Accumulation of non-biodegradable chemicals at higher trophic levels
Neutralisation of acidic water by dissolved minerals
Enrichment of water with nutrients leading to excessive algal growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enrichment of water with nutrients leading to excessive algal growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is a process characterized by the excessive enrichment of water bodies with minerals and nutrients, primarily **Nitrates** and **Phosphates**.
 
• These nutrients act as fertilizers, stimulating the rapid and dense growth of **phytoplankton** and **algae** on the water surface, a phenomenon known as an **Algal Bloom**.
 
• The dense algal layer prevents **sunlight** from reaching submerged aquatic plants, inhibiting their **photosynthesis** and leading to their death.
 
• When these algae eventually die, **aerobic bacteria** (decomposers) consume large quantities of **Dissolved Oxygen** (DO) to break down the organic matter.
 
• This massive consumption of oxygen leads to **hypoxia** (oxygen depletion), which creates **dead zones** where fish and other aquatic organisms cannot survive, ultimately causing a collapse of the **aquatic ecosystem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biological Magnification (Biomagnification)**:

 
 
• This refers to the increasing concentration of persistent, **non-biodegradable** toxic substances, such as **DDT** or **Mercury**, at higher **trophic levels** in a food chain.
 
• Unlike eutrophication, which involves nutrient enrichment, biomagnification involves the accumulation of **pollutants** in the tissues of organisms.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Nutrients**:
 
 
• **Agricultural Runoff**: Excess chemical **fertilizers** washed into lakes and rivers.
 
• **Sewage and Wastewater**: Domestic and industrial waste containing **phosphates** from detergents.
 
 
 
• **Types of Eutrophication**:
 
 
• **Natural Eutrophication**: A slow, centuries-long process of a lake aging.
 
• **Cultural (Anthropogenic) Eutrophication**: Accelerated nutrient enrichment caused specifically by **human activities**.
